sessionHandle.identity: ACP backends persist acpSessionId plus a pinned acpWrapperVersion (<backend>@<version>) in conversations.extra; a fresh spawn resumes the same session through session/load replay, or self-heals through wrapper-mismatch history replay.

adapters.note: The ACP backend owns its session; resumability is proven by the persisted session id bound to a pinned wrapper version, not by process liveness.

sessionHandle.identity: Wayland Core resumes a conversation with --resume <conversationId>; the durable transcript and session state are producer-owned and Desktop only seeds best-effort history.

adapters.note: Core session capture is producer-quiescence dependent; the quiescence lease is deferred to #896, so Core cannot enter the cohort and fails closed until the producer-owned successor is accepted.

sessionHandle.identity: Gemini persists only sessionMode (approval) and the selected model; it exposes no backend conversation session handle, so a live Gemini process is never evidence of a resumable session.

adapters.note: Gemini has no backend session/handle to capture or resume; it is truthfully degraded to read-only and excluded from the cohort rather than normalized into success.

storageAuthorities.note: Desktop SQLite (wayland.db) is a separately inventoried Desktop-owned storage authority; it is never a backend session adapter and cannot substitute for one.
Office and artifact workspaces are separately inventoried Desktop-owned storage; they never stand in for backend session/handle authority.
